$comment: Hero sections family. scripts/build-registry.mjs turns every entry in `items` into a registry item at /r/<name>.json; apps/docs/scripts/build-catalog.mjs turns them into /templates/<name> pages. License tier per item lives in source/licenses.json.
title: Hero sections
intro: Three hero sections with HeiGin's own brand: a studio portfolio wall of case studies, a light hero with a live agent panel, and a dark hero with a dashboard that settles into place. Each installs on its own.
previewNote: Shown with the HeiGin brand and sample content. The wall's case studies and client logos are placeholders, and its cover photos are not part of the download.
requirements: A "@/" import alias pointing at your source root (the shadcn default)
setup: Install the item with the shadcn CLI. It adds the files listed above plus heroes-core, which every hero shares.
Import the stylesheet once in your global CSS, after Tailwind and the HeiGin tokens: @import "tailwindcss"; @import "@heigin/ui/styles.css"; @import "@heigin/ui/tailwind.css"; @import "./heroes.css";
Edit lib/heroes-config.ts: brand, copy, links and the integrations each hero shows all live there.

items.name: heroes-core
items.title: Heroes core
items.description: Shared foundation for the hero sections: the content config, the brand mark (the HeiGin mark until you set your own logo), service logos, small utilities and the stylesheet.
items.responsive: Shared pieces only; each hero documents its own breakpoints.
replaceable: Brand: the HeiGin mark and name until brand.logoSrc and brand.name are set.

Service logos are each owner's marks (from the CC0 Iconify logos set). The archive and tracer heroes show them as integrations and the wall shows them as sample clients; keep only the tools you really work with and the clients you really have.

items.name: hero-wall
items.title: Studio portfolio wall
items.description: A portfolio hero for a studio: a tilted masonry wall of case-study covers, each a cover image with the client's logo, that pans against the pointer while a "Book a call" pill trails the cursor. Scrolling flattens the wall and slides "Selected work" over it, with client, project, services and year under each cover.
items.responsive: The wall fills the viewport at every width. The nav pills collapse to the demo button below 768px, the cursor pill is mouse-only, and the work grid stacks to one column on phones.
replaceable: The case studies in wall.caseStudies are sample content. Replace the clients, projects, services and years with your own work, and only show a client's logo if you have worked with them.
Cover photos come from wall.covers. The download ships none and falls back to gradient covers; the photos in the preview are not part of the template.
The pause button and the reduced-motion setting both stop the drift and the pointer tilt.

items.name: hero-archive
items.title: Product window over an archive
items.description: A light hero: headline and pill buttons, a riveted promo plate, and a product window with a live AgentTaskTrail from @heigin/ui, over an archive collage that drifts and blurs out at the edges.
items.responsive: The promo plate shows from 1280px and the agent panel from 1024px. Below 640px the window drops its sidebar and the headline steps down to 30px.
replaceable: The collage tiles are drawn in code on the client (technical drawings, punch cards, prints); no images ship with it.
The window's workspace, invoice and agent messages are sample data in hero-archive.tsx.

items.name: hero-tracer
items.title: Dark dashboard that settles
items.description: A dark hero: the headline blurs in while a tilted dashboard of agent runs settles flat, a new run streams in, and a "Works with" row shows the integrations. Uses local dark values on top of the HeiGin tokens.
items.responsive: Below 768px the dashboard drops its sidebar and the table scrolls sideways inside its card; the headline steps down to 38px.
replaceable: Run titles, models, costs and timings are sample data in hero-tracer.tsx.
Model and integration logos come from the config (tracer.models, tracer.worksWith).
